taste.name: Information Density over Visual Leisure
taste.trigger: When designing the document viewer for constrained mobile views...
taste.decision: Chose tight spacing and a small body font (14px) over whitespace-heavy layouts.
taste.reason: Users need to see maximum scanned content and tool options without scrolling endlessly on small screens.

taste.name: Document-First Neutrality
taste.trigger: When deciding how to frame the user's uploaded images...
taste.decision: Chose a strictly neutral canvas (white backgrounds, minimal accent colors) over vibrant UI.
taste.reason: Users require a predictable, distraction-free canvas so that any document type is legible.
evidence: Accent blue (37, 99, 235) used only for primary actions

taste.name: Typography Restriction
taste.trigger: When choosing how to handle diverse text elements...
taste.decision: Chose a single font family (Plus Jakarta Sans) in multiple weights over a multi-font pairing.
taste.reason: Restricting the type system to one family creates immediate visual cohesion and reduces user cognitive load.
evidence: 38 out of 49 font instances (77%) are Plus Jakarta Sans

taste.name: Layout Directness
taste.trigger: When deciding how to organize the content panels...
taste.decision: Chose a cardless, direct flow over secondary containers.
taste.reason: Removing container boundaries minimizes visual noise and keeps focus strictly on the document processing tools.
evidence: Layout flows directly on the page background
